confirmed.title: With the default config the change test never fires on a clean content swap, and every detection test overrides the default
confirmed.detail: Reviewed vmf_field.py md5 c8efc86d; the file changed twice while I was reviewing it. The current defaults are fast_memory=0.9 (line 87), change_score='raw' and change_thr=0.5 (lines 90-91). With these, the fast bucket holds about 10 views and the slow bucket absorbs new content at about 1 view per view, so c = 1 - cos(S,F) stays small. For an orthogonal, noise-free swap A->B after h views of A, the largest c ever reached is 0.222 (h=4), 0.283 (h=8), 0.443 (h=20) and 0.645 (h=50). So Gaussians with 20 or fewer history views can never reach thr=0.5, and fire (line 329) stays false. Nothing catches this, because every test that checks detection sets fast_memory=0.5: tests/test_change.py:41 ('mechanics test: short memory'), tests/test_pipeline_dryrun.py:66 and tests/test_gsplat_gpu.py:114. scripts/run_mapping.py:36 and :134-136 build FieldConfig() and never call calibrate_change_threshold. The other score is also unsafe at the shared default threshold. Under no change, change_score='normalized' has mean about 0.4-0.9, so thr=0.5 flags 25-29% (d=64) and 55-59% (d=16) of STATIC Gaussians. This holds at every noise level.
confirmed.fix: Do not ship a fixed default change_thr. Either make run_mapping (and the mock) run the mapping pass with change_thr=inf and then call calibrate_change_threshold(), or default change_thr=None and raise until it is calibrated. Give 'normalized' its own threshold scale (above 1). Add one test that checks detection with FieldConfig() defaults.

confirmed.title: The normalized change score's null E0[1-cos(S,F)] leaves out the shared-view term, so it is not scale-free and its bias depends on how many views a Gaussian has
confirmed.detail: Each view i is split between the two buckets: weight b_i stays in F and a_i = w_i - b_i leaks into S. The buckets are disjoint in mass but not in observations. Under no change, E[S.F] = rho^2 (A B - sum a_i b_i) + q sum a_i b_i. _null_dissimilarity (lines 379-394) uses only rho^2 A B, which overstates the null dissimilarity. The missing sum a_i b_i equals fC - fB2, and both are already tracked (lines 314-317). Measured mean c_norm under no change, default fast_memory=0.9, d=16: 0.27 at view 6, 0.30 at view 10, 0.41 at view 20, 0.52 at view 30 and 0.61 at view 40. Adding the term gives 0.97-1.00 at every age. The bias also depends on beta: the mean is 0.97 / 0.68 / 0.44 for fast_memory 0.5 / 0.8 / 0.9, using test_change's own setup. So one threshold on the normalized scale gives very different false-positive rates for young and old Gaussians. The test docstring (tests/test_change.py:119-122) blames a 'ratio-of-expectations approximation' with a 'roughly constant bias'. Both points are wrong: the bias comes from the missing term, and it is not constant. The test's bound 0.4 < n_lo < 1.4 hides it. A smaller issue: the 1e-3 floor on E0 is hit for 93% of very coherent content (noise 0.02), where c_norm averages 0.19 against 0.41 at other noise levels.
confirmed.fix: In cos0, use numerator rho2 + x*(fC - fB2)/(A*B) instead of rho2, with x = q - rho2. The denominator terms rho2 + x*A2/A^2 and rho2 + x*fB2/B^2 are already right. Then tighten the test to about 0.85 < mean < 1.15 at fast_memory 0.5, 0.8 and 0.9, and at two history lengths.

verdict.evidence:
I could not refute it. The math is wrong as claimed, and two independent checks confirm it. I rate it minor, not major, because only the non-default ablation path uses this code.

**Why the formula is wrong.** The recursion is at usplat/vmf_field.py:306-317: keep = beta^w, Rs += (1-keep)*Rf, Rf = keep*Rf + w*u. So each view i sits in both buckets: weight b_i = w_i * prod_{t>i} beta^{w_t} in F, and a_i = w_i - b_i in S. The buckets are disjoint in mass, not in observations. The module docstring at lines 35-38 says they are "DISJOINT", which is wrong in this sense.

Under no change, E[S.F] = rho2*(AB - sum a_i b_i) + q*sum a_i b_i. The code's cos0 at lines 392-393 uses only rho2 in the numerator. The denominators are right, since nS = A^2/A2 and nF = B^2/fB2. The missing sum a_i b_i equals fC - fB2, and both are already tracked.

**Check 1: formula alone, true rho2 plugged in, no field code.** Script: scratchpad/review/verify-math-1/indep_null.py, log indep_null.log. It compares Monte Carlo E0[1-cos] with each closed form. Ratio MC / code formula:
- beta 0.5: 0.71 at V=6, 0.95 at V=40
- beta 0.8: 0.38 at V=6, 0.80 at V=40
- beta 0.9: 0.28 at V=6, 0.61 at V=40

The ratio is nearly the same at noise 0.3, 0.5 and 0.9, so it depends on age and beta, not on noise. With the shared-view term added, the ratio is 0.98-1.05 in all 36 cases. Example, beta 0.9, noise 0.5, V=6: MC 0.1264, code 0.4508, fixed 0.1219.

**Check 2: end to end through the field.** Script: field_null.py, log field_null.log. Setup: change_score="normalized", no change, noise 0.5, d=16, float64. Mean c_norm by history length:

| beta | V6 | V10 | V20 | V30 | V40 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.5 | 0.74 | 0.81 | 0.90 | 0.93 | 0.95 |
| 0.8 | 0.38 | 0.47 | 0.65 | 0.74 | 0.80 |
| 0.9 | 0.27 | 0.30 | 0.42 | 0.52 | 0.60 |

A single threshold at the pooled q99 (1.061, default beta 0.9) gives these false-positive rates: 0.000 at V6, 0.000 at V10, 0.002 at V20, 0.013 at V30 and 0.040 at V40. So the bias is not constant, and the test docstring's "roughly constant bias" explanation (tests/test_change.py:119-122) is wrong. The loose bound 0.4 < n_lo < 1.4 (test_change.py:151) hides it.

**Secondary floor claim: not re-run by me.** The reviewer's null_check_b09.log shows E0 hitting the 1e-3 floor in 93.2% of cases at noise 0.02 (c_norm mean 0.19). That fits the true E0 there being below 1e-3.

**Why minor.** _null_dissimilarity is called only when change_score == "normalized" (vmf_field.py:323-324). The default is "raw" (line 90), and the calibrated raw-quantile path never uses it. It does affect a recorded result, though: docs/reports/2026-09-28-method-completion/attempts/03-normalized-score.md blames AUROC 0.75 -> 0.60 on correlated views alone. That ablation ran with this age-dependent mis-normalization, so the formula should be fixed and the ablation re-run before that row or its explanation is used in the paper.

The fix is as the reviewer proposed: numerator rho2 + x*(fC - fB2)/(A*B). The docstring formula at lines 41-42 needs the same change.

confirmed.title: The default epistemic score 1/(1+Kish) ignores view weight, so a Gaussian only grazed in 5 views gets the same u_epi as one fully seen in 5 views
confirmed.detail: epistemic='kish' is the default (line 76) and computes 1/(1+W1^2/W2) (lines 470-471). Kish is invariant to scaling the weights. Five views at w=3.3e-4 (0.01 px of splat mass per 640x480 view, W1 = 0.0016 views) give Kish = 5 and u_epi = 0.1667, the same as five full views at w=1. The W2 > 1e-12 guard (line 141) adds a jump: at w=3.3e-7 per view, Kish = 0 and u_epi = 1.0. The support read-out already guards against this with min(Kish, W1) (line 147); its docstring says 'many weak views count as little evidence'. In views mode that min always equals W1, because w <= 1 implies Kish >= W1. The epistemic read-out has no such guard. The effect: EFEPlanner.epistemic_value treats grazed Gaussians as well observed, and u_epi is lowest for Gaussians whose mu* rests on almost no evidence, which hurts the epistemic AUSE. P1 (mean_direction) handles the same Gaussians correctly: their E[mu] is about 0.
confirmed.fix: Default epistemic to 1/(1+support) = 1/(1+min(Kish, W1)); in views mode that is 1/(1+W1). Keep pure Kish only as the NormLift baseline row.

- Unverified: for Gaussians whose weight stays well below 1 in every view, the default reduces toward the trivial visible-view-count baseline (F11).

   - +7 GB of headroom while a MASt3R batch is queued
   - `set_per_process_memory_fraction`

Free memory is also not re-checked after the lock is taken. The header comment at line 10 says "the memory check protects them" (the USGLoc jobs), which overstates what the script does.

   `UAGS JOB STARTED (should have waited: run_7scenes present)` gate rc=0.

rejected.title: Change score's null depends on per-Gaussian dispersion: with the per-scene calibrated threshold, false alarms fall only on ambiguous static Gaussians (20% vs 0%)
rejected.detail: c = 1 - cos(S, F) has a noise floor that grows as agreement drops. calibrate_change_threshold takes a single q99 over all Gaussians' mapping-pass c_max (l.370). In a scene with 90% coherent (sigma .1) and 10% ambiguous (sigma .6) static Gaussians, the mapping-pass c_max medians are 0.032 vs 0.338 and the calibrated threshold is 0.413. In the update pass, 20.3% of the ambiguous static Gaussians fire and 0.0% of the coherent static ones do; real changes on coherent ones fire at 100%. The fired Gaussians have their aleatoric evidence reset. With the default readmit_depth and no depth they also stay flagged 'changed' permanently. So the change channel re-detects aleatoric ambiguity, which is the confusion the two-channel design is meant to remove. It directly inflates the Tab II static false-alarm row. The i.i.d. normalized score was the attempted fix; it is marked measured-negative in the docstring. Note: vmf_field.py changed during review (fast_memory 0.5 -> 0.9, calibrate_change_threshold added). With the older beta=0.5 and the fixed threshold 0.5, 98% of static Gaussians with centred agreement about 0.38 fired.
rejected.fix: Calibrate per Gaussian or per agreement stratum, e.g. a quantile of c conditional on binned Kish agreement or support. Or gate the change test on slow-bucket agreement >= r_min and report ambiguous Gaussians as 'undetermined'. At minimum, report the false-alarm rate stratified by u_ale.
